name: Overhead
short: A drone survey firm whose survey lines draw themselves over real aerial photos as you scroll.
long: A two-person drone survey outfit in slate and cloud with one hi-vis orange for booking. The first screen is a real aerial film flown over Peak District fields. Below it, three real stills show what the client actually gets back: half-metre contours and a boundary on a field, a measured roof with six numbered defects, and cut and spoil on a building site, each drawing itself over the photo as you scroll. Four fixed prices carry straight into an enquiry that checks the postcode and says who rings back and when.
proves: A survey firm can show what it hands over, not just a gallery of aerial photos.
story: Drone operators all show the same thing: pretty aerial photographs. What they are paid for is measurement, so the page draws the survey over the photo, the way the client will see it.
